answer: An unstirred nebula settles, and the settling is the tell. Each identity seals one chamber holding an aerosol nebula whose particle sizes decay on a set curve unless a key-committed stirrer works it nonstop. Auditors fire a set zephyr pulse through the chamber at its station's tide phase, reading outflow turbidity: a curve matching the decay model passes, a settled or freshly stirred curve fails. Tide phases scatter the pulses, so no operator services chambers in sequence. One honest agent runs one chamber, one stirrer; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 chambers and 1,000 stirrers, none ever idle.
